title: Fughetta of the Paper Paddock
brief: A baroque-style fughetta for harpsichord and strings, about two and a half minutes: a subject with a clear head and tail answered by each voice in turn, a countersubject that keeps its shape, episodes in sequence to related keys, a stretto over a dominant pedal near the end, and a firm cadence.

sections.intent: Subject in the harpsichord, answer in the violin, subject in the viola, answer in the cello, the countersubject kept in its own voice each time; a codetta closes it
Head and countersubject in a sequence rising by fourths: IV - V - I of F major
Subject in F major (harpsichord), answer in C (violin), subject in the bass
Head and countersubject falling by thirds, F - Dm - Bb, then D, the dominant of G minor
Subject in G minor (viola), answer in D minor (violin), subject in the bass (cello)
Gm - F - Dm - Bb in the sequence, then E diminished and the dominant A
Stretto: five entries, answer and subject alternating one bar and a half apart, over a dominant pedal
The subject in the bass in the tonic, the countersubject above it
The third episode with violin and viola, the ascent to the dominant, a firm cadence with the third raised

association.whole: On a wet afternoon someone folds a savanna out of rice paper on a table by a window with a wooden lattice and a shutter: a paddock of paper animals, a paper rowboat on a bowl of water with a shoal of paper fry under it. A spider lets one thread down across the lattice, then a second and a third along the same path, and a fourth, so that four threads hang there answering one another. A magpie hops along the sill, takes a bright scrap of the web at a time and carries it from pane to pane, from room to room of the paddock. Grains of rice scatter and settle. At the end every animal huddles into one corner of the paddock, the heel of a foot is planted on one note, the shutter is pulled to, and the last light through the lattice goes out in one firm chord.

gives.what: the fugue follows the scene: the exposition lays the four threads one by one; three episodes are the magpie carrying scraps; the stretto is the huddle; the cadence is the shutter

subject = the thread: a head that leaps D-A-D across the lattice and a tail that folds the paper back (a falling scale, then the neighbour-note cell 3-2-1-2 twice, a step lower each time); countersubject = the rice: even eighth notes in thirds and sixths that keep their shape

the paddock is a fence of related keys: F major (the relative) and G minor (the subdominant) as its two rooms; the huddle is a dominant pedal the voices crowd over; the last chord lets the light in with a raised third
the rowboat is the cello's paired oar strokes (root-third-root, then A low-high-low-high) under the episodes and the pedal; the fry are the sixteenth-note flicks in the tail
rice paper and plucked wire: the harpsichord on its single Flemish 8-foot stop, with a solo violin, viola and cello, each a single player, as in a room for four
the shutter: the room is a near one (clarity C80 +8 dB), the lines easy to follow, little hall around them

plan.identity: A fughetta in D minor made from two bars of subject (a rising D-A-D head folded back by a neighbour-note tail) and two bars of countersubject (rice-grain eighths), passed between harpsichord, violin, viola and cello, sequenced in the episodes and crowded together in a stretto over a dominant pedal.

high_point.means: entries one bar and a half apart over a held dominant, the violin's subject an octave higher (D5-D6) in bar 40, the cello's pedal in octave strokes, ending in the dominant that the return resolves

sections.differs: four entries, each in a new voice; the countersubject stays beside each
the head and the countersubject in sequence, the viola resting
the subject in the relative major, three voices only
harpsichord and viola as the pair; the violin rests
the viola begins the entries; the subdominant colour (Eb, F#)
falling sequence, then the climb to the dominant
entries overlap; the cello holds the pedal
the subject in the bass, in the tonic, after the pedal
the third episode with other voices, then the cadence

decisions: vertical: seven places, each sounding twice because the harpsichord's left hand doubles the cello. Three were changed: bar 7, where the viola's held F3 rubbed the cello's E3 for an eighth, now moves to C4 half a beat earlier; bars 33 and 49, where the last eighth pair of the falling head put Bb4 over the bass A2, now end the head on a held C5. The other four (bars 35, 38, 41, 51) are a Bb eighth, entered and left by step on a weak half beat, over the dominant A: the flat ninth of the dominant, a colour that D minor takes in the style, and it is part of the subject's own falling head in bars 38 and 41; kept.

revision_history.note: first draft: four-voice fughetta, 53 bars, harpsichord on one 8-foot register

answered the review's collisions (bars 7, 33, 49); the stretto made the high point by registration (the harpsichord's 8' + 4' on its entries and the last chord), by 102 against 76-84 in velocity and by +2 dB; the coda and the cadence lowered (r1 measured the coda 2.8 dB above the stretto and the cadence at -1.2 dBFS, holding the whole master 1.6 dB under its target); the violin and viola labelled melody parts, the viola raised 2 dB and the cello lowered 1 dB; target loudness -18 LUFS

r2 measured the stretto 5.5 dB above the episodes (-14.6 against -19.5 to -21.8 LUFS, the violin and viola stems near -16): lowered to 96 in velocity and +1 to +1.5 dB; the cello's bass lines in the episodes 4 velocity steps and its support lines under entries 4 more (r2: the cello 0.9 dB under the melody group in the G minor entries, the left hand 1.9 dB), the left hand 2 dB lower

attack times measured on the r3 stems at the first entries (10% of the note's early peak: violin 23 ms, cello 19 ms, viola 39 ms before its -40 ms offset): offsets of -20 ms (violin) and -15 ms (cello) so that the entries sit on the beat with the harpsichord; the penultimate note of the final cadence trilled, written out from the upper note (baroque.md)
